title: Which nest should the teacher build? Five real nest shapes, plus the ladder's current plan
question: Which of these looks like the nest you want the ants to dig? Pick one (or say what to change). Also: do the flat, low chambers (1-5) look right to you, against the tall rooms the ladder plans now (6)?
context_md:
These are drawn targets, not simulations. Nothing has dug them. Each one is a real species' nest as seen in vertical section (ant-farm view), from plaster and metal casts (Tschinkel) and glass-sided lab nests, fitted to our 256 x 128 box with the ground at row 64.

- **Scale:** our ant is 2 cells long. Passages are drawn 4 cells wide (your 'passage ~4'). Chambers are 5 cells tall (2.5 body lengths), which is twice the real height so they stay readable.
- **The main finding:** real chambers are flat lenses. They are 1-2 body lengths high at every size, and 3-20 times wider than tall. They grow wider, never taller. The ladder's planned chambers (8-16 cells tall, panel 6) are 3-5 times taller than any real one.
- **The mound is drawn to hold all the dug soil.** In a 2D slice nothing spreads into a third dimension, so the mound's area equals the nest's. That is why every mound is a wide, flat ring about 8 cells tall. The gap beside the mouth keeps the inner slope from sliding back into the hole, and real ants drop beyond the crest for the same reason.
- **Which to pick matters for teaching:** shapes made by simple local rules are easier for the brain to learn. Examples: 'dig down from a chamber's edge, widen at the bottom' (5); 'stop the roof at about body height' (1, 4, 5); 'bud when the room stops being crowded' (3). Shape 2 (the tangle) is the hardest to teach.
- Tunnel paths for 2, 3 and 5 are my reading of written descriptions. Treat them as the gist, not exact.

items.label: 1 Harvester stack
items.caption: Florida harvester ant: zig-zag shaft, wide flat chambers on alternating sides, big near the top and small deep down

items.label: 2 Garden-ant tangle
items.caption: Lasius: 2-4 wandering, branching galleries with swellings, one loop, no trunk

items.label: 3 Round room that buds
items.caption: Messor in 2D lab nests: today's shaft into one room that buds, then grows galleries as ants are added

items.label: 4 Carpenter shallow
items.caption: Camponotus socius: long top chambers that curl up to just under the surface, wedge-shaped lenses below, mound on one side

items.label: 5 Staircase stack
items.caption: Aphaenogaster: each shaft leaves one chamber's edge and lands in the next one's centre. The only real family that fits the box at true scale

items.label: 6 Ladder plan today
items.caption: dig-rung-design steps 10-11: chambers 8-16 cells tall, width at least height. For comparison
